title: Attention Is All You Need
content: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
Google Brain · Google Research · University of Toronto
31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2017)
A new sequence transduction architecture based solely on attention mechanisms.
presenter_notes: Greet the audience, introduce yourself, and frame the paper in one sentence: this work replaces recurrence and convolution with pure attention.

title: Background: Sequence Transduction is Transforming Language Technology
content: Sequence transduction models power critical applications: machine translation, text summarization, speech recognition.
Neural machine translation has revolutionized how we communicate across languages.
Traditional approaches rely on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) processing sequences step-by-step.
Attention mechanisms have become integral to sequence modeling, enabling dependency modeling regardless of distance.
The field is rapidly evolving with demands for faster training and better long-range dependency capture.
presenter_notes: Start with the importance of sequence transduction. Make the audience care about this research area by highlighting real-world applications like translation services they use daily.

title: Problem: Sequential Computation Limits Model Efficiency
content: RNNs have inherently sequential nature that precludes parallelization within training examples.
At longer sequence lengths, memory constraints limit batching across examples.
Convolutional approaches require operations that grow with distance between positions (linearly or logarithmically).
Learning dependencies between distant positions remains difficult with existing architectures.
State-of-the-art models require significant training time and computational resources.
Ensemble methods are often needed to achieve best results, multiplying computational costs.
presenter_notes: Transition from field importance to specific problem. Help audience understand why sequential computation is a fundamental bottleneck that limits both training speed and model quality.

title: Computational Complexity: Why Sequential Models Struggle
content: Recurrent models require O(n) sequential operations where n is sequence length.
This limits training efficiency especially for long sequences.
Maximum path length of O(n) makes learning long-range dependencies difficult.
Convolutional approaches improve parallelization but still have path length growing with distance.
The fundamental constraint remains despite improvements through factorization tricks.
Need for a architecture that enables full parallelization while capturing global dependencies.

title: Solution Overview: The Transformer Architecture
content: First sequence transduction model based entirely on attention mechanisms.
Eschews recurrence entirely and relies solely on attention for global dependencies.
Follows encoder-decoder structure using stacked self-attention and point-wise fully connected layers.
Allows significantly more parallelization than RNN or CNN-based architectures.
Achieves state-of-the-art translation quality after training for as little as twelve hours.
Core innovation: multi-headed self-attention replaces recurrent layers in encoder-decoder architectures.
presenter_notes: Introduce the Transformer at a high level. Emphasize that this is the first model to completely eliminate recurrence and convolution, relying purely on attention mechanisms.

title: Methodology: Complete Transformer Architecture
content: Encoder composed of N=6 identical layers with two sub-layers each.
First sub-layer: multi-head self-attention mechanism.
Second sub-layer: position-wise fully connected feed-forward network.
Decoder also has N=6 layers but adds third sub-layer for encoder-decoder attention.
Residual connections around each sub-layer followed by layer normalization.
All sub-layers produce outputs of dimension d_model=512.
Input/output embeddings multiplied by √d_model before adding positional encoding.

figure_reference.caption: The Transformer - model architecture showing encoder-decoder structure with stacked self-attention and feed-forward layers

presenter_notes: Walk through the architecture diagram. Point out the encoder stack on left, decoder stack on right, and the three types of attention mechanisms. Explain residual connections and layer normalization.

title: Technical Core: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
content: Core attention function maps queries and key-value pairs to output vectors.
Computed as weighted sum of values where weights come from query-key compatibility.
Scaling by √d_k counteracts large dot product magnitudes.
Prevents softmax from pushing into regions with extremely small gradients.
Enables parallel computation of attention across all query positions simultaneously.
Fundamental building block that replaces sequential RNN computations.

figure_reference.caption: Scaled Dot-Product Attention (left) and Multi-Head Attention with parallel attention layers (right)

equation_reference.context:
In practice, we compute the attention function on a set of queries simultaneously, packed together into a matrix Q. The keys and values are also packed together into matrices K and V . We compute the matrix of outputs as: Attention(Q, K, V ) = softmax(QKT

presenter_notes: Explain the attention formula. The scaling factor is crucial - without it, large dot products push softmax into saturation. This mechanism allows the model to focus on relevant parts of the input regardless of distance.

title: Technical Innovation: Multi-Head Attention
content: Allows model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces.
Linearly projects queries, keys, and values h times with different learned projections.
Performs attention in parallel on each projected version.
Model uses h=8 parallel attention heads with d_k=d_v=d_model/h=64.
Concatenates outputs from all heads and applies final linear projection.
Single attention head would average information, inhibiting specialized learning.
Different heads learn to perform different tasks related to syntactic and semantic structure.

equation_reference.context: Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. With a single attention head, averaging inhibits this. Where the projections are parameter matrices WQi ∈ R^dmodel×dk, WKi ∈ R^dmodel×dk, WVi ∈ R^dmodel×dv and WO ∈ R^hdv×dmodel.

presenter_notes: Explain why multi-head is essential. Each head can focus on different aspects - some on syntax, others on semantics. This parallel attention mechanism is what gives Transformer its power.

title: Technical Details: Feed-Forward Networks & Positional Encoding
content: Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks applied to each position separately and identically.
Consists of two linear transformations with ReLU activation: FFN(x) = max(0, xW_1+b_1)W_2+b_2.
Dimensionality: d_model=512, inner-layer d_ff=2048.
Model contains no recurrence or convolution, so needs positional information injected.
Positional Encoding uses sine and cosine functions of different frequencies.
Each dimension corresponds to a sinusoid with wavelengths forming geometric progression.
Allows model to learn to attend by relative positions for any fixed offset.

equation_reference.context: In addition to attention sub-layers, each of the layers in our encoder and decoder contains a fully connected feed-forward network, which is applied to each position separately and identically. This consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between. The dimensionality of input and output is dmodel = 512, and the inner-layer has dimensionality df f = 2048.

presenter_notes: Cover two key components. Feed-forward networks add non-linearity at each position. Positional encoding is clever - it injects order information without learned parameters, using fixed sine/cosine functions.

title: Technical Details: Positional Encoding Formula & Training
content: Positional Encoding formula: PE(pos,2i) = sin(pos/10000^(2i/d_model)).
PE(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/10000^(2i/d_model)).
Wavelengths form geometric progression from 2π to 10000·2π.
Training uses Adam optimizer with β1=0.9, β2=0.98, ε=10^-9.
Learning rate schedule increases linearly for first 4000 warmup steps.
Then decreases proportionally to inverse square root of step number.
This adaptive schedule stabilizes training in early steps while allowing convergence later.

equation_reference.latex:
P E(pos,2i) = sin(pos/100002i/dmodel)
P E(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/100002i/dmodel)
equation_reference.context: In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: where pos is the position and i is the dimension. That is, each dimension of the positional encoding corresponds to a sinusoid. The wavelengths form a geometric progression from 2π to 10000 · 2π. We chose this function because we hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions.

presenter_notes: Complete the technical picture with positional encoding formula and training details. The learning rate schedule is important - warmup prevents early instability, then gradual decrease enables fine-tuning.

title: Training Optimization: Learning Rate Schedule
content: Learning rate formula: lrate = d_model^(-0.5) · min(step_num^(-0.5), step_num · warmup_steps^(-1.5)).
Corresponds to increasing learning rate linearly for first warmup_steps training steps.
Then decreasing it thereafter proportionally to inverse square root of step number.
Used warmup_steps = 4000 for all experiments.
This schedule is crucial for training deep Transformer models effectively.
Combined with Adam optimizer enables efficient training of the architecture.
Allows model to reach convergence faster than traditional fixed learning rate approaches.

title: Key Results: English-to-German Translation Performance
content: Transformer (big) achieves 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German.
Outperforms best previously reported models including ensembles by over 2.0 BLEU.
Training takes 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs.
Base model achieves 27.3 BLEU at fraction of training cost.
3.3·10^18 FLOPs vs 7.7·10^19 for ConvS2S Ensemble.
Represents significant efficiency gains while achieving superior quality.
First single model to outperform all previous ensembles on this task.

table_reference.caption: Table 2: The Transformer achieves better BLEU scores than previous state-of-the-art models on the English-to-German and English-to-French newstest2014 tests at a fraction of the training cost

presenter_notes: Highlight the main results. Transformer achieves 28.4 BLEU on EN-DE, beating all previous models including ensembles. Training cost is dramatically lower - this is the key breakthrough.

title: Key Results: English-to-French Translation & Training Efficiency
content: Transformer (big) achieves 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-French.
New single-model state-of-the-art, surpassing previous best ensemble of 41.29.
Training cost: 2.3·10^19 FLOPs vs 1.2·10^21 for ConvS2S Ensemble.
Represents less than 1/4 training cost of previous state-of-the-art.
Base model at 3.3·10^18 FLOPs outperforms all previous single models.
Training time: 3.5 days on eight GPUs vs weeks for previous approaches.
Demonstrates Transformer achieves state-of-the-art quality at fraction of computational cost.
presenter_notes: Continue with EN-FR results. Emphasize the training efficiency - less than 1/4 the cost while achieving better quality. This makes state-of-the-art translation accessible to more researchers.

title: Ablation Study: Architecture Design Choices
content: Single-head attention (h=1) performs 0.9 BLEU worse than 8-head base.
Multi-head attention is essential for optimal performance.
Reducing attention key size d_k hurts quality (25.1 vs 25.8 BLEU).
Compatibility determination between queries and keys is not easy.
Bigger models perform better: d_model=1024 achieves 26.0 BLEU vs 24.5 for d_model=256.
Dropout is very helpful: 0.1 rate optimal, 0.0 drops to 24.6 BLEU.
Sinusoidal vs learned positional embeddings produce nearly identical results.

table_reference.caption: Table 3: Variations on the Transformer architecture

presenter_notes: Walk through the ablation study. Multi-head is critical - single head loses 0.9 BLEU. Model size matters. Dropout prevents overfitting. These design choices were carefully validated.

title: Generalization: English Constituency Parsing Results
content: Transformer generalizes well beyond machine translation to parsing tasks.
With WSJ only training (40K sentences), achieves 91.3 F1.
Outperforms most previous models and approaches best of 91.7.
In semi-supervised setting (17M sentences), achieves 92.7 F1.
Surpasses all previous semi-supervised models (best previous 92.1).
Outperforms RNN sequence-to-sequence models even in small-data regimes.
Proves architecture generalizes well to tasks with strong structural constraints.

title: Analysis: Attention Mechanism Interpretability
content: Self-attention yields more interpretable models than black-box RNN approaches.
Individual attention heads learn to perform different tasks.
Some heads handle syntactic dependencies, others handle semantic relationships.
Attention patterns reveal model learns meaningful linguistic structures without explicit supervision.
Long-distance dependencies are captured effectively - verb 'making' attends to 'more difficult'.
Anaphora resolution: attention heads connect 'its' to antecedents with sharp focus.
This interpretability is a valuable side benefit of the self-attention mechanism.

figure_reference.caption: Attention mechanism following long-distance dependencies in encoder self-attention layer 5, showing verb 'making' attending to complete phrase 'making...more difficult'

presenter_notes: Show the attention visualization. Point out how the model captures long-distance dependencies. This interpretability makes Transformer more transparent than RNNs - we can see what the model is attending to.

title: Analysis: Specialized Attention Head Functions
content: Different attention heads exhibit specialized behavior patterns.
Some heads focus on syntactic dependencies within sentences.
Others handle semantic coreference and anaphora resolution.
Attention distributions are sharp and focused on relevant words.
Layer 5 heads show particularly clear linguistic structure learning.
Model learns these patterns without explicit linguistic supervision.
Demonstrates self-attention can discover meaningful linguistic representations.

figure_reference.caption: Two attention heads in layer 5 involved in anaphora resolution, showing sharp attention from word 'its' to antecedents

presenter_notes: Show the anaphora resolution example. The word 'its' clearly connects to its antecedent. Different heads learn different functions - this specialization is emergent from training, not designed.

title: Conclusion: Core Contributions Summary
content: First sequence transduction model based entirely on attention mechanisms.
Replaces recurrent layers with multi-headed self-attention in encoder-decoder architectures.
Achieves new state-of-the-art on WMT 2014 English-to-German (28.4 BLEU) and English-to-French (41.8 BLEU).
Outperforms all previously reported ensembles on English-to-German translation.
Trains significantly faster than recurrent or convolutional architectures.
Self-attention yields more interpretable models with learned syntactic and semantic structures.
Generalizes well to other tasks like English constituency parsing.
presenter_notes: Summarize the main contributions. Emphasize this is a paradigm shift - pure attention replaces recurrence. Better quality, faster training, more interpretable.

title: Future Work & Broader Impact
content: Apply attention-based models to other tasks beyond translation and parsing.
Extend Transformer to problems with input/output modalities other than text.
Potential applications: images, audio, video processing.
Investigate local restricted attention mechanisms for large inputs/outputs.
Make generation less sequential to further improve efficiency.
Code available at github.com/tensorflow/tensor2tensor for community adoption.
This architecture opens new directions for sequence modeling research.

presenter_notes: Discuss future directions. The Transformer architecture is general - can apply to images, audio, video. Code is open source, enabling community research. This work fundamentally changed NLP.
